records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וַתִּלְבַּ֤שׁ אֶסְתֵּר֙ מַלְכ֔וּת וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֞ד בַּחֲצַ֤ר בֵּית־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַפְּנִימִ֔ית נֹ֖כַח בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְ֠הַמֶּלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֞ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֤א מַלְכוּתוֹ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמַּלְכ֔וּת נֹ֖כַח פֶּ֥תַח הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And it was on the day the third, and put on Esther royalty, and stood in [the] court of [the] house of the king the inner, in front of [the] house of the king; and the king [was] sitting on his royal throne in [the] house of the royalty, in front of [the] entrance of the house.
pieces: On the third day Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, in front of the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the throne room, facing the entrance.

L.1: And it came about on the third day that Esther put on royalty and stood in the inner court of the king's house, in front of the king's house. And the king was sitting on his royal throne in the royal house, facing the entrance of the house.

R.1: On the third day of the fast, Esther put on her royal robes and went and stood in the inner courtyard of the palace, in front of the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne inside, facing the doorway.

decisions.choice: the third day: the third day of the fast
decisions.reason: Esther had asked for a fast of three days (4:16). She goes to the king on the third day, before it is over or as it ends.

decisions.choice: put on royalty: put on her royal clothing
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "put on royalty"; the word for royalty stands for royal robes (compare 6:8; 8:15). Esther comes not as a mourner but as queen.

decisions.choice: the inner court and the throne room facing the entrance
decisions.reason: The throne faced the entrance, so the king could see whoever stood in the court outside. Esther stands where she will be seen, in the inner court that no one could enter uncalled (4:11).

decisions.choice: her royal robes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "royalty" means here; Literal keeps the bare word.

decisions.choice: of the fast
decisions.reason: Readable links the third day back to the fast of 4:16.

records.heading: Esther's banquet and Haman's gallows

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִרְא֨וֹת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־אֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֗ה עֹמֶ֨דֶת֙ בֶּֽחָצֵ֔ר נָשְׂאָ֥ה חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַיּ֨וֹשֶׁט הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּ֗ר אֶת־שַׁרְבִ֤יט הַזָּהָב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָד֔וֹ וַתִּקְרַ֣ב אֶסְתֵּ֔ר וַתִּגַּ֖ע בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הַשַּׁרְבִֽיט׃ס
records.gloss: And it was, as saw the king Esther the queen standing in the court, she lifted up favor in his eyes, and held out the king to Esther the scepter of gold which [was] in his hand; and drew near Esther and touched the top of the scepter.
pieces: When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, she won his favor, and he held out to her the gold scepter in his hand. So Esther came near and touched the tip of the scepter.

L.2: And it came about, when the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, that she gained favor in his eyes, and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. And Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter.

R.2: When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, he was pleased with her. He held out to her the gold scepter that was in his hand. So Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter.

decisions.choice: she lifted up favor in his eyes: she won his favor
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used when Esther first won favor with Hegai and the king (2:9, 15, 17). Her life depends on it (4:11).

decisions.choice: the scepter held out and touched: the king receives her and spares her
decisions.reason: Holding out the scepter was the sign that someone who came uncalled would live (4:11). By touching its tip Esther accepts the king's pardon and is received.

decisions.choice: he was pleased with her
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom from the king's side, which says the same thing in plain words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַה־לָּ֖ךְ אֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה וּמַה־בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֛ךְ עַד־חֲצִ֥י הַמַּלְכ֖וּת וְיִנָּ֥תֵֽן לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said to her the king, What [is] to you, Esther the queen? And what [is] your request? Up to half of the kingdom, and it will be given to you.
pieces: The king said to her, "What is it, Queen Esther? What is your request? Even if it is half the kingdom, it will be given to you."

L.3: And the king said to her, "What is it to you, Queen Esther? And what is your request? Even to half of the kingdom, it will be given to you."

R.3: The king asked her, "What is the matter, Queen Esther? What do you want? I will give you anything, even half my kingdom."

decisions.choice: up to half of the kingdom: a royal promise of great generosity
decisions.reason: The phrase is a king's formula of generous promise, not a legal offer to divide the realm (5:6; 7:2; compare Mark 6:23).

decisions.choice: what is it to you: what is troubling you, what do you want
decisions.reason: The king guesses that only something serious would bring Esther in uncalled.

decisions.choice: What is the matter ... What do you want?
decisions.reason: Readable puts the king's two questions in everyday words.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶסְתֵּ֔ר אִם־עַל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ט֑וֹב יָב֨וֹא הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהָמָן֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֶל־הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֥יתִי לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Esther, If on the king [it is] good, let come the king and Haman today to the feast that I have made for him.
pieces: Esther replied, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to a banquet I have prepared for him."

L.4: And Esther said, "If it is good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast that I have prepared for him."

R.4: Esther answered, "If it pleases you, Your Majesty, please come today with Haman to a banquet I have prepared for you."

decisions.choice: the king and Haman: Esther invites her enemy too
decisions.reason: Esther does not make her request at once, and she includes Haman in the invitation. The text does not give her reasons; the story will set the accusation at a feast, with Haman present (7:6).

decisions.choice: feast: a banquet with drinking
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to drink" and is used of every feast in the book (1:3; 2:18; 5:6). Feasts mark the turning points of the story.

decisions.choice: let the king and Haman come today: the first letters of four words spell the divine name
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition noticed that the first letters of these four Hebrew words spell the divine name YHWH, and some manuscripts mark them. Whether this is meant is uncertain; the book itself never names God.

decisions.choice: If it pleases you, Your Majesty ... for you
decisions.reason: Esther speaks to the king in the third person, as was courtly. Readable turns this into a direct address, which is how such polite speech sounds in English.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מַהֲרוּ֙ אֶת־הָמָ֔ן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר אֶסְתֵּ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְהָמָ֔ן אֶל־הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשְׂתָ֥ה אֶסְתֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And said the king, Hurry Haman, to do the word of Esther. And came the king and Haman to the feast that had made Esther.
pieces: The king said, "Bring Haman at once, so that we may do as Esther asks." So the king and Haman went to the banquet Esther had prepared.

L.5: And the king said, "Bring Haman quickly, to do as Esther has said." And the king and Haman came to the feast that Esther had prepared.

R.5: The king said, "Bring Haman here quickly, so we can do what Esther asks." So the king and Haman went to the banquet Esther had prepared.

decisions.choice: hurry: bring quickly
decisions.reason: The verb means to make haste or to hurry someone; here the king orders Haman fetched at once (compare 6:14, where Haman is hurried to the second feast).

decisions.choice: so that we may do as Esther asks
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "to do the word of Esther" has no stated subject; Balanced and Readable supply "we", the king and Haman.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּר֙ בְּמִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן מַה־שְּׁאֵלָתֵ֖ךְ וְיִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֑ךְ וּמַה־בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֛ךְ עַד־חֲצִ֥י הַמַּלְכ֖וּת וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃
records.gloss: And said the king to Esther at [the] feast of the wine, What [is] your petition? And it will be given to you. And what [is] your request? Up to half of the kingdom, and it will be done.
pieces: As they were drinking wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your petition? It will be granted to you. What is your request? Even if it is half the kingdom, it will be done."

L.6: And the king said to Esther at the feast of wine, "What is your petition? It will be given to you. And what is your request? Even to half of the kingdom, it will be done."

R.6: While they were drinking wine, the king asked Esther again, "What do you want? I will give it to you. What are you asking for? I will do it, even if it is half of my kingdom."

decisions.choice: the feast of wine: the drinking that followed the meal
decisions.reason: At a Persian banquet the wine was served after the food; this was the moment for talk and requests (7:2).

decisions.choice: petition and request: two words for the same thing, asked twice
decisions.reason: The two words are near synonyms; the king repeats his offer from verse 3 in a fuller, more formal way (7:2).

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Readable adds "again" because the king repeats what he asked in verse 3.

records.gloss: And answered Esther and said, My petition and my request:
pieces: Esther answered, "My petition and my request is this:

L.7: And Esther answered and said, "My petition and my request:

R.7: Esther answered, "This is what I want to ask:

decisions.choice: my petition and my request: Esther begins, and then asks for a second feast
alternatives: she begins to state her request and then holds back
decisions.reason: The verse stops after these words, and verse 8 goes on with an invitation instead of the request itself. It may be a formal opening ("my request is this"), or a sign that Esther starts and then delays. Either way, the real request waits for the second feast (7:3).

records.source: אִם־מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֜ן בְּעֵינֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְאִם־עַל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ ט֔וֹב לָתֵת֙ אֶת־שְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י וְלַעֲשׂ֖וֹת אֶת־בַּקָּשָׁתִ֑י יָב֧וֹא הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְהָמָ֗ן אֶל־הַמִּשְׁתֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם וּמָחָ֥ר אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה כִּדְבַ֥ר הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: If I have found favor in [the] eyes of the king, and if on the king [it is] good to grant my petition and to do my request, let come the king and Haman to the feast that I will make for them, and tomorrow I will do according to [the] word of the king.
pieces: If I have found favor with the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and do what I request, let the king and Haman come tomorrow to the banquet I will prepare for them. Then I will do as the king has said."

L.8: If I have found favor in the eyes of the king, and if it is good to the king to grant my petition and to do my request, let the king and Haman come to the feast that I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do according to the word of the king."

R.8: If the king is pleased with me and is willing to give me what I ask, then please come with Haman to another banquet I will prepare for you tomorrow. Then I will tell you what I want, as you have asked."

decisions.choice: I will do according to the word of the king: I will answer the king's question
decisions.reason: The king has asked twice what she wants (verses 3, 6). Esther promises that at the next feast she will do as he says and make her request known.

decisions.choice: a second feast: the request is delayed
decisions.reason: Esther does not explain why she waits. Between the two feasts the story turns: Haman builds the gallows and the king's sleepless night leads to Mordecai's honor (5:14-6:14).

decisions.choice: tomorrow, moved to the invitation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "tomorrow" in the last clause; Balanced and Readable move it to the invitation, which also takes place tomorrow, to make the time clear.

decisions.choice: I will tell you what I want, as you have asked
alternatives: I will do according to the word of the king
decisions.reason: Readable says what Esther's promise means.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֤א הָמָן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא שָׂמֵ֖חַ וְט֣וֹב לֵ֑ב וְכִרְאוֹת֩ הָמָ֨ן אֶֽת־מָרְדֳּכַ֜י בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְלֹא־קָם֙ וְלֹא־זָ֣ע מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וַיִּמָּלֵ֥א הָמָ֛ן עַֽל־מָרְדֳּכַ֖י חֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went out Haman on the day the that joyful and good of heart; and as saw Haman Mordecai in [the] gate of the king, and he did not rise and did not tremble from him, and was filled Haman toward Mordecai [with] rage.
pieces: Haman went out that day happy and in high spirits. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and Mordecai neither stood up nor showed any fear of him, Haman was filled with rage against Mordecai.

L.9: And Haman went out that day joyful and good of heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai in the king's gate, and he did not rise and did not tremble before him, Haman was filled with rage against Mordecai.

R.9: Haman left the banquet that day happy and in a very good mood. But then he saw Mordecai at the palace gate. Mordecai did not stand up for him or show any fear of him. Haman became furious with Mordecai.

decisions.choice: good of heart: in good spirits
decisions.reason: A "good heart" is a cheerful mood, often from food and wine (1:10; Judges 16:25; 1 Samuel 25:36).

decisions.choice: he did not rise and did not tremble: Mordecai shows him no respect and no fear
decisions.reason: Mordecai is back at his place in the gate. He not only refuses to bow (3:2) but does not even stand up or show fear before the man who has decreed his people's death.

decisions.choice: rage: burning anger
decisions.reason: The same word as in 3:5. Haman's joy turns to anger at the sight of one man.

records.source: וַיִּתְאַפַּ֣ק הָמָ֔ן וַיָּב֖וֹא אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־אֹהֲבָ֖יו וְאֶת־זֶ֥רֶשׁ אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And restrained himself Haman and came to his house; and he sent and brought his friends and Zeresh his wife.
pieces: Nevertheless, Haman controlled himself and went home. He sent for his friends and his wife Zeresh.

L.10: But Haman restrained himself and came to his house. And he sent and brought his friends and Zeresh his wife.

R.10: But Haman kept his anger to himself and went home. He called together his friends and his wife Zeresh.

decisions.choice: restrained himself: held back his feelings
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Joseph holding back his tears (Genesis 43:31; 45:1). Haman keeps his anger hidden for now.

decisions.choice: Zeresh his wife
decisions.reason: Zeresh is named only in Esther (5:14; 6:13). She and the friends act as Haman's counselors, as the king's advisers did in 1:13-15.

records.source: וַיְסַפֵּ֨ר לָהֶ֥ם הָמָ֛ן אֶת־כְּב֥וֹד עָשְׁר֖וֹ וְרֹ֣ב בָּנָ֑יו וְאֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר גִּדְּל֤וֹ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְאֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְּׂא֔וֹ עַל־הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְעַבְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And recounted to them Haman the glory of his riches and the abundance of his sons, and all that had made him great the king, and that he had lifted him up above the princes and the servants of the king.
pieces: Haman boasted to them about his great wealth and his many sons, and about all the ways the king had honored him and raised him above the king's officials and servants.

L.11: And Haman recounted to them the glory of his riches and the number of his sons, and all how the king had made him great and how he had lifted him up above the princes and the servants of the king.

R.11: Haman bragged to them about how rich he was and how many sons he had. He told them about all the ways the king had honored him, and how the king had given him a higher place than all the other leaders and officials.

decisions.choice: the number of his sons: a sign of honor
decisions.reason: Many sons were counted a blessing and a source of standing (Psalm 127:3-5). Haman had ten sons (9:7-10).

decisions.choice: how the king made him great and lifted him up: the words of 3:1
decisions.reason: Haman repeats the very verbs used of his promotion in 3:1. He recounts what the reader already knows, which shows his pride.

decisions.choice: princes and servants (Literal); officials and servants (Balanced); leaders and officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: The two words follow the project's usual choices for the king's high officers and his servants at court.

decisions.choice: boasted about his great wealth (Balanced); bragged about how rich he was (Readable)
alternatives: recounted the glory of his riches
decisions.reason: "Recounted" here is a proud telling; Balanced and Readable make that plain. Literal keeps "the glory of his riches".

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ הָמָן֒ אַ֣ף לֹא־הֵבִיאָה֩ אֶסְתֵּ֨ר הַמַּלְכָּ֧ה עִם־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖תָה כִּ֣י אִם־אוֹתִ֑י וְגַם־לְמָחָ֛ר אֲנִ֥י קָֽרוּא־לָ֖הּ עִם־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Haman, Also, not did let come Esther the queen with the king to the feast that she had made [anyone] except me; and also for tomorrow I [am] invited by her with the king.
pieces: Haman added, "What is more, Queen Esther let no one but me come with the king to the banquet she gave. And tomorrow she has invited me again, along with the king.

L.12: And Haman said, "Moreover, Queen Esther let no one come with the king to the feast that she had prepared except me. And tomorrow also I am invited by her, together with the king.

R.12: Haman went on, "And that is not all. Queen Esther invited no one except me to come with the king to her banquet. She has invited me again tomorrow, together with the king.

decisions.choice: no one except me: Haman takes Esther's invitation as a special honor
decisions.reason: Haman sees only the honor. The reader knows Esther is about to accuse him at the feast (7:6), so his boasting is full of irony.

decisions.choice: Moreover (Literal); What is more (Balanced); And that is not all (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "also" adds one more honor to the list in verse 11.

records.source: וְכָל־זֶ֕ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ שֹׁוֶ֖ה לִ֑י בְּכָל־עֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֤י רֹאֶה֙ אֶת־מָרְדֳּכַ֣י הַיְּהוּדִ֔י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּשַׁ֥עַר הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And all this not it [is] worth to me in every time that I [am] seeing Mordecai the Jew sitting in [the] gate of the king.
pieces: Yet none of this satisfies me as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

L.13: Yet all this is worth nothing to me every time that I see Mordecai the Jew sitting in the king's gate."

R.13: But none of this makes me happy while I still see that Jew Mordecai sitting at the palace gate."

decisions.choice: worth: to be equal to, to satisfy
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Haman used in 3:8 ("it is not worth the king's while"). Now nothing he has is worth anything to him while Mordecai sits at the gate.

decisions.choice: Mordecai the Jew: Haman names him by his people
decisions.reason: Haman's hatred is tied to Mordecai's being a Jew (3:4-6), and the book uses this title for Mordecai repeatedly (6:10; 8:7; 9:29, 31; 10:3).

decisions.choice: satisfies me (Balanced); makes me happy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "it is not worth to me" means in plain English.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לוֹ֩ זֶ֨רֶשׁ אִשְׁתּ֜וֹ וְכָל־אֹֽהֲבָ֗יו יַֽעֲשׂוּ־עֵץ֮ גָּבֹ֣הַּ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּה֒ וּבַבֹּ֣קֶר׀אֱמֹ֣ר לַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיִתְל֤וּ אֶֽת־מָרְדֳּכַי֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבֹֽא־עִם־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֶלהַמִּשְׁתֶּ֖ה שָׂמֵ֑חַ וַיִּיטַ֧ב הַדָּבָ֛ר לִפְנֵ֥י הָמָ֖ן וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָעֵֽץ׃פ
records.gloss: And said to him Zeresh his wife and all his friends, Let them make a tree high, fifty cubits, and in the morning speak to the king and let them hang Mordecai on it, and go with the king to the feast joyful. And was good the word before Haman, and he made the tree.
pieces: His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows built, {{units:about 75 feet|fifty cubits}} high, and in the morning ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go with the king to the banquet and enjoy yourself." Haman liked the idea, and he had the gallows built.

L.14: And Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, "Let them make a gallows fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king, and let them hang Mordecai on it. Then go with the king to the feast joyful." And the thing was good in Haman's sight, and he made the gallows.

R.14: His wife Zeresh and all his friends told him, "Have a gallows built, {{units:about 75 feet|fifty cubits}} high. In the morning, ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then you can go to the banquet with the king and be happy." Haman liked this idea, so he had the gallows built.

decisions.choice: gallows: a tall wooden pole on which a body was hung, or a man impaled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is simply "tree" or "wood". Persian kings impaled enemies on stakes, as Herodotus records of Darius (Histories 3.159), and "hanging on a tree" in Scripture can mean exposing a body after death (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Joshua 10:26). Whether Mordecai was to be hanged alive or impaled is not certain; "gallows" keeps the picture of a tall structure for execution.

decisions.choice: fifty cubits high: about 75 feet
decisions.reason: A cubit was about 18 inches. A pole so high would be seen across the city; the size shows the scale of Haman's spite.

decisions.choice: in the morning speak to the king: they take the king's consent for granted
decisions.reason: Zeresh and the friends assume the king will agree, as he did to the decree (3:10-11). Haman goes to the palace early the next morning for this purpose (6:4).

decisions.choice: about 75 feet, with fifty cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the cubit; Balanced and Readable give the modern measure with the original unit as a reader setting.

decisions.choice: Haman liked the idea
alternatives: the thing was good in Haman's sight
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the idiom plainly; Literal keeps it.
